lines.text: Not round. Not lumpy. Actual cubes.
Up to a hundred of them, every single night.
lines.caption: Up to 100 of them, every single night.

lines.text: For years, nobody knew how they did it.
Then scientists studied wombat intestines, and found the trick.
The gut walls aren't equally stretchy. Some parts are stiff, others are soft. Squeeze through that, and you get corners.
Wombats stack them on rocks to mark their turf. And cubes don't roll away.
The research even won an Ig Nobel Prize.
Sounds fake? It's true. Follow for more.
